microtheory.name: control_systems_foundation
microtheory.definition: Classical + modern control theory. Feedback, plants, controllers, stability, transfer functions, state-space, PID, frequency response, root locus, Nyquist + Bode + Lyapunov, nonlinear control. The mathematical framework for steering dynamical systems toward desired behavior. Grounds the feedback_control subsystem of Jabberwock's runner/brain design — the substrate's drives, corrections, regulators map directly onto controllers, error signals, and stability margins.

concepts.name: plant_control
concepts.definition: The system being controlled. Receives control input + produces output. Has dynamics. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's Mt being regulated.

concepts.name: controller
concepts.definition: Component computing control input from error signal. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's correction-firing handler.

concepts.name: setpoint
concepts.definition: Desired output value. Reference signal. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's drive target.

concepts.name: process_variable
concepts.definition: Measured output of plant. Compared with setpoint. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ-state value.

concepts.name: error_signal
concepts.definition: e(t) = setpoint - process_variable. Drives controller. Substrate analogue: substrate's ΔF / frustration.

concepts.name: control_signal
concepts.definition: u(t) — controller's output to plant. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction action.

concepts.name: feedback_loop
concepts.definition: Closed loop: error → controller → plant → sensed output → error. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-correction loop.

concepts.name: open_loop
concepts.definition: No feedback. Controller outputs based on setpoint alone. Brittle. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded reflexes without correction.

concepts.name: closed_loop
concepts.definition: Feedback present. Self-correcting. Standard control architecture. Substrate analogue: substrate's full drive ensemble.

concepts.name: pid_control
concepts.definition: Proportional-Integral-Derivative. u(t) = Kp·e + Ki·∫e dt + Kd·de/dt. Workhorse of industrial control. ~95% of control loops worldwide. Substrate analogue: substrate's three-component correction drive.

concepts.name: proportional_term
concepts.definition: Kp·e. Responds to current error magnitude. Larger Kp → faster + more aggressive. Substrate analogue: substrate's immediate-correction strength.

concepts.name: integral_term
concepts.definition: Ki·∫e dt. Eliminates steady-state error. Accumulates persistent error. Substrate analogue: substrate's sustained-frustration accumulator.

concepts.name: derivative_term
concepts.definition: Kd·de/dt. Predictive — responds to rate of error change. Damps oscillation. Substrate analogue: substrate's anticipation handler.

concepts.name: ziegler_nichols_tuning
concepts.definition: 1942. Empirical PID tuning: increase Kp until oscillation, then Kp ← 0.6·Ku, Ki ← 2Kp/Pu, Kd ← Kp·Pu/8. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-coefficient empirical tuning.

concepts.name: integral_windup
concepts.definition: Integral term saturates during prolonged actuator limits. Causes overshoot. Anti-windup mechanisms reset. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction over-accumulation failure.

concepts.name: transfer_function
concepts.definition: G(s) = output(s)/input(s) in Laplace domain. Captures dynamics in single algebraic expression. Substrate analogue: substrate's input-output operator characterization.

concepts.name: laplace_transform
concepts.definition: F(s) = ∫₀^∞ f(t)e^{-st} dt. Transforms ODEs into algebraic equations. Foundation of classical control. Substrate analogue: substrate's frequency-domain analysis.

concepts.name: frequency_response
concepts.definition: How system responds to sinusoidal input at each frequency. Magnitude + phase per frequency. Substrate analogue: substrate's response across input timescales.

concepts.name: bode_plot
concepts.definition: Magnitude (dB) + phase vs log frequency. Visual stability + performance assessment. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-frequency response visualization.

concepts.name: nyquist_criterion
concepts.definition: Encirclement test for stability via Nyquist plot. Substrate analogue: substrate's loop-stability check.

concepts.name: root_locus
concepts.definition: How closed-loop poles move as gain varies. Tool for controller tuning. Substrate analogue: substrate's parameter-sweep stability analysis.

concepts.name: gain_margin
concepts.definition: How much gain can increase before instability. Stability robustness measure. dB. Substrate analogue: substrate's tolerance to drive amplification.

concepts.name: phase_margin
concepts.definition: Additional phase lag before instability at 0 dB crossover. Substrate analogue: substrate's delay tolerance.

concepts.name: stability_bibo
concepts.definition: Bounded-Input Bounded-Output stability. Standard for LTI systems. Substrate analogue: substrate's bounded response guarantee.

concepts.name: lyapunov_stability
concepts.definition: Lyapunov 1892. System stable iff there exists V(x) > 0 with dV/dt ≤ 0. Direct method for nonlinear stability. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-attractor stability check.

concepts.name: lyapunov_function
concepts.definition: Energy-like scalar V(x) decreasing along trajectories. Proves stability without solving ODE. Substrate analogue: substrate's Hamiltonian as Lyapunov function.

concepts.name: asymptotic_stability
concepts.definition: Solutions converge to equilibrium as t → ∞. Stronger than mere stability. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin attraction.

concepts.name: exponential_stability
concepts.definition: ||x(t)|| ≤ K·||x(0)||·e^{-λt}. Quantitative convergence rate. Substrate analogue: substrate's convergence rate bound.

concepts.name: state_space_model
concepts.definition: ẋ = Ax + Bu, y = Cx + Du. Modern (post-1960) standard. Multi-input multi-output capable. Substrate analogue: substrate's full-state representation.

concepts.name: state_vector
concepts.definition: x ∈ R^n. Compact description of system memory. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ-vector.

concepts.name: controllability
concepts.definition: Can reach any state from any other via control input. Kalman test: rank of controllability matrix = n. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-reachability.

concepts.name: observability
concepts.definition: Can determine state from output history. Dual of controllability. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspectability.

concepts.name: duality_controllability_observability
concepts.definition: Kalman 1960. The two are mathematical duals. Substrate analogue: substrate's action-observation duality.

concepts.name: pole_placement
concepts.definition: Choose feedback gain to place closed-loop poles at desired locations. Requires full controllability. Substrate analogue: substrate's equilibrium-design.

concepts.name: linearization
concepts.definition: Approximate nonlinear system as linear near operating point via Taylor expansion. Foundation of local control. Substrate analogue: substrate's local-basin linearization.

concepts.name: nonlinear_control
concepts.definition: Beyond LTI assumptions. Lyapunov methods, sliding mode, backstepping, feedback linearization. Substrate analogue: substrate's nonlinear dynamics.

concepts.name: sliding_mode_control
concepts.definition: Drive system to sliding surface; stay on it. Robust to disturbance. Bang-bang character. Substrate analogue: substrate's hard-decision boundaries.

concepts.name: feedback_linearization
concepts.definition: Cancel nonlinearity via feedback. Effective when model exact. Substrate analogue: substrate's nonlinearity-canceling correction.

concepts.name: backstepping
concepts.definition: Recursive Lyapunov-based design. For systems with strict-feedback structure. Substrate analogue: substrate's nested-correction design.

concepts.name: discrete_time_control
concepts.definition: Sampled-data control. Z-transform replaces Laplace. Substrate analogue: substrate's tick-discretized control.

concepts.name: z_transform
concepts.definition: X(z) = Σ x[n] z^{-n}. Discrete-time analog of Laplace. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-tick analysis.

concepts.name: zero_order_hold
concepts.definition: DAC reconstruction holding each sample constant. Adds delay. Substrate analogue: substrate's tick-period commitment.

concepts.name: aliasing_control
concepts.definition: Sampling above Nyquist required. High-frequency disturbances fold into baseband. Substrate analogue: substrate's tick-rate constraint.

concepts.name: disturbance_rejection
concepts.definition: Suppress effects of unmeasured disturbances. Loop gain at disturbance frequency determines suppression. Substrate analogue: substrate's noise-robust correction.

concepts.name: tracking_performance
concepts.definition: How well process variable follows setpoint changes. Rise time, settling time, overshoot, steady-state error. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-target tracking.

concepts.name: robustness
concepts.definition: Performance under model uncertainty. Robust if maintains performance across parameter variation. Substrate analogue: substrate's prior-uncertainty tolerance.

concepts.name: settling_time
concepts.definition: Time to enter + remain within ε of setpoint. Performance metric. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction convergence time.

concepts.name: overshoot
concepts.definition: Maximum excursion beyond setpoint as fraction of step size. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction overcorrection.

concepts.name: feedforward_control
concepts.definition: Use measured disturbance directly. No feedback delay. Combined with feedback. Substrate analogue: substrate's anticipation contribution.

concepts.name: cascade_control
concepts.definition: Inner loop nested in outer. Inner faster. Improves disturbance rejection. Substrate analogue: substrate's nested-correction hierarchy.

concepts.name: ratio_control
concepts.definition: Maintain ratio between two variables. Process control common. Substrate analogue: substrate's coupled-variable maintenance.

concepts.name: smith_predictor
concepts.definition: Model-based dead-time compensation. Eliminates effect of input-output delay. Substrate analogue: substrate's anticipation correction for delay.

concepts.name: saturation_actuator
concepts.definition: Real actuators have limits. Saturation degrades performance + causes wind-up. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-magnitude bound.

concepts.name: dead_zone
concepts.definition: Range where small inputs produce no output. Substrate analogue: substrate's threshold-below-which no action.

concepts.name: hysteresis
concepts.definition: Output depends on history. Common in actuators. Substrate analogue: substrate's state-dependent response.

rules.name: feedback_is_self_correction
rules.head: Jabberwock builds a regulator
rules.body: feedback (sensed-output → error → correction) is the foundational pattern. Open-loop control fails on disturbed or model-uncertain plants.

rules.name: pid_handles_most_loops
rules.head: Jabberwock designs a controller for a stable plant
rules.body: PID is the default starting point. P alone for fast simple loops; PI for steady-state-error elimination; PID for predictive damping.

rules.name: stability_required_for_useful_control
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates a control design
rules.body: stability (Lyapunov, BIBO, or pole-placement) is a prerequisite. Unstable closed loop is worse than no control.

rules.name: controllability_observability_dual
rules.head: Jabberwock builds a state-feedback controller
rules.body: controllability is required to place closed-loop poles. Observability is required if state must be estimated from output. Kalman 1960 — they're mathematical duals.

rules.name: real_disturbances_drive_robustness_requirement
rules.head: Jabberwock's controller will face real disturbances + model errors
rules.body: robust design (gain margin > 6 dB, phase margin > 45°) is required to maintain performance under uncertainty.
